events.summary: The satellite first saw signs of burned vegetation in the Sierra de Gredos foothills across Ávila and Madrid on 26 July 2026, in an area of mostly trees and grassland. The affected patch kept growing over five satellite passes and was at its largest, about 81 square kilometres, on the latest pass on 30 October 2026, so it may still be spreading. The radar showed leaves and branches had disappeared and stayed gone, and the detection is fairly confident (0.82 on a 0-to-1 scale).

Confidence in this reading is moderate (0.77), and the satellite revisits every 12 days.
